text:
customer-success: FYI - Priority customer (ACME) reporting p99 spikes ~6-8s during peak billing window, says API returns 500s and throttled attaches. Escalating to oncall.

ashley: saw the ticket, added logs + timeline. customer reports issue started 2025-04-07 09:12 UTC, impacts only Dedicated pools with priority queue. attaching their sample trace.

sre-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-pool-priority-queue: p99 latency > 5s for 3 consecutive mins for pool: eu-west-prod-priority. incidents/INC-2025-142 auto-created -> https://incidents.internal/INC-2025-142 :warning:

kevin: can you paste the trace or a small repro? need request ids + attach_id to find warmup behavior. initial suspicion: attach queue jitter + cold GPU start.

customer-success: pasted snippet: `req=ch_01Fxx attach_id=att-3745 status=500 error="attach_timeout" duration_ms=8123`

maria: pulling metrics now. Quick checks: 1) min_pool for that dedicated tier is 0, 2) fairshare configured with strict priority buckets, 3) autoscale spike at 09:10 caused many new attaches. Likely minpool=0 + throttled image pulls -> coldgpu warmup cascade.

kevin: +1. Also seeing a burst of concurrent attach attempts (fanout) at 09:11:59 -> attach rate jumped x12. Kernel image pull latency spiked (image-pull p95 14s).

jonathan: oncall here. Immediate mitigations: a) bump min_pool to 2 for eu-west-prod-priority, b) enable temporary fallback routing to lower-priority prewarmed hostpool, c) short-term increase attach retry backoff to reduce thundering herd. I'll run the commands now.

jonathan: running:
```
# emergency: increase min pool
redwoodctl pools update eu-west-prod-priority --min-instances 2 --scale-policy emergency
# enable fallback route
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --pool eu-west-prod-priority --fallback-pool eu-west-shared-prewarm
```

sre-bot: Deploy task queued: rollout-id=rl-7876, ETA 18s.

ashley: customer is on call, told them we're applying mitigations and will monitor.

kevin: while that rolls, useful to capture attach logs on the pool nodes: `kubectl logs -l pool=eu-west-prod-priority --since=10m`. Also check node-level OOM/eviction and image-pull errors. snippet I saw: `E0420 09:11:59.123 kubelet: Failed to pull image "redwood/gpu-runtime:2025-04-07": context deadline exceeded`.

maria: extracted histograms: attach_latency_ms p50=120, p95=3200, p99=7800 (before mitigation). image_pull p95=14000. After bumping min_pool (09:12:40) p99 dropped to ~1900 within 90s.

jonathan: rollback plan if regressions: 1) revert min_pool change, 2) disable fallback routing. But we need root fix: prewarm policy for priority customers + keep minpool>=1 across billing windows.

kevin: long-term action items: write an autoscale guard that rate-limits concurrent attach spikes per pool; add image_pull cache warming to our nodes; add a probe to failover to GPU-warm hosts sooner. I'll open a GH issue with repro steps and telemetry snippets.

ashley: customer accepted the mitigation, saw improved p99 in their short tests. They asked for ETA on a permanent fix. I promised follow-up by EOD. :thumbsup:

maria: adding playbook to support/playbooks/priority-pool-warmup.md (draft): steps to detect attach-fanout, increase min_pool, enable fallback, gather logs, and notify devs. Will link to GH issue.

jonathan: noted. Also adding an immediate alert tweak: fire if attach_rate_surge AND image_pull_p95>5s to catch this earlier.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2025-142 updated: mitigation applied, monitoring for 30m.

kevin: for the repro in the GH issue include this minimal script (simulates attach fanout):
```
for i in $(seq 1 150); do
  curl -s -X POST https://eu-west.api.redwood.ai/v1/attach -d '{"model":"gpt-large","priority":"customer-acme"}' &
done
wait
```

customer-success: I'll schedule a post-mortem + follow-up call with ACME tomorrow. Thanks team.

jonathan: closing loop: p99 back to normalish (<=2s) after interventions, continuing to watch. If any regression ping @jonathan directly. :white_check_mark:
